name: Mentaya vs SimplePractice
title: Mentaya vs SimplePractice: OON Billing Service vs Full EHR Comparison
description: Compare Mentaya (out-of-network billing service) and SimplePractice (practice management EHR). Understand how these complementary tools serve different purposes for therapy practices.

summary.bottom_line: Mentaya and SimplePractice serve different functions and are complementary. SimplePractice is a complete practice management EHR (scheduling, billing, notes, portal). Mentaya is a specialized out-of-network billing service that files claims for clients and offers payment advances. You need an EHR like SimplePractice to run your practice; Mentaya adds OON reimbursement support for clients.

key_differences.pricing_model: Mentaya (5% of reimbursements) vs SimplePractice (monthly subscription)
key_differences.who_pays: Mentaya (clients pay fee) vs SimplePractice (provider pays)

sections.heading: Mentaya vs SimplePractice: Overview
sections.content: Mentaya and SimplePractice are not competitors—they solve different problems. SimplePractice is a comprehensive practice management EHR handling scheduling, client portal, in-network insurance billing, documentation, and telehealth. Mentaya is a specialized service that submits out-of-network claims for clients and offers payment advances so clients pay less upfront. OON therapists often use SimplePractice for practice management and add Mentaya to improve the client payment experience.

sections.heading: Pricing Comparison
sections.content: SimplePractice costs $49-99/month paid by the provider for complete practice management. Mentaya charges 5% of reimbursements paid by the client (not the provider). Key distinction: Mentaya's fee comes from clients' insurance reimbursements, not your practice budget. Mentaya Pay can advance clients money before insurance pays out, reducing their upfront cost. Different billing scenarios, different pricing models.

sections.heading: Feature Differences
sections.content: SimplePractice provides: appointment scheduling, client intake portal, in-network claims submission, superbills for OON, progress notes, telehealth, and e-prescribing. Mentaya provides: OON claim submission for clients, benefit verification, claim tracking, appeals support, and Mentaya Pay advances (clients pay less upfront, get reimbursed later). SimplePractice creates superbills; Mentaya files them and manages the reimbursement process.

recommendations.when: You're in-network and need practice management, OR you're OON and clients can handle filing superbills themselves
You're OON and want to make therapy more affordable for clients—Mentaya's advances mean clients pay less upfront while waiting for reimbursement
Never—Mentaya only handles OON billing. You still need an EHR like SimplePractice for scheduling, documentation, and practice operations

faqs.q: Does Mentaya replace SimplePractice for OON practices?
faqs.a: No. Mentaya only handles OON claim submission and reimbursement advances. You still need an EHR like SimplePractice for scheduling, notes, client management, and running your practice. Mentaya is an add-on, not a replacement.

faqs.q: How is Mentaya different from SimplePractice's OON billing?
faqs.a: SimplePractice generates superbills for clients to submit themselves. Mentaya files claims for clients, tracks them, handles appeals, and offers payment advances so clients pay less upfront. Mentaya manages the entire OON reimbursement process.

Clients pay Mentaya's 5% fee from their insurance reimbursements, not the therapist. This differs from SimplePractice where the provider pays the subscription. Adding Mentaya doesn't increase your practice costs.

Mentaya Pay advances clients money before insurance reimburses them. Clients pay less out-of-pocket at the time of service. When insurance pays out, Mentaya recovers the advance plus their fee. This makes OON therapy more affordable upfront.
